summary: Techniques for managing conversation history and context to prevent exceeding token limits while maintaining coherence

content.overview: Context management addresses the challenge of maintaining long-running conversations within fixed context window limits (typically 128K-200K tokens). As conversations grow, the combined context (system prompt + history + current query + tool results) can exceed limits, causing failures or degraded performance. Core strategies: (1) Sliding window (keep recent N messages), (2) Summarization (compress old history), (3) Memory formation (extract key facts), (4) Prioritization (rank by relevance). Production systems increasingly use hybrid approaches. Critical metric: Smart memory systems like Mem0 cut token costs 80-90% while improving response quality 26% vs. basic history management.
keyPoints: Sliding window: Maintain fixed-size context (e.g., last 10-15 messages verbatim), drop oldest messages as new ones arrive - simplest but loses historical context
Summarization: Periodically compress old messages (e.g., every 10 turns) into summaries, keep recent messages verbatim - balances history retention with context limits
Hierarchical summarization: Multi-level compression (messages → conversation segments → overall summary) preserves essential information at different granularities
Memory formation: Extract specific facts, preferences, decisions (not compress everything) for long-term storage - more intelligent than raw summarization
Context prioritization: Rank information by relevance, include only top-k most relevant items in context - recency + semantic similarity are common scoring factors
CRITICAL TRADEOFF: More context history improves coherence but increases cost/latency and risks exceeding limits - find optimal balance for use case
Production best practice: Keep last 10-15 exchanges verbatim + summarize older content + extract key facts to separate memory store

warnings: Summarization adds cost and latency - each summarization is an additional LLM call, compounds quickly in long conversations
Summary quality varies - LLMs can drop important details, introduce errors, or generate vague summaries that lose critical context
Aggressive truncation breaks conversation coherence - user references 'the bug we discussed earlier' but that context was dropped
Memory extraction requires careful design - poor fact extraction logic misses critical information or pollutes memory with irrelevant details
Recency bias can be wrong - sometimes oldest context is most important (e.g., initial requirements), prioritize intelligently
Don't summarize recent messages - keep last 10-15 verbatim; summarizing recent exchanges degrades quality noticeably
bestPractices: Start simple (sliding window), add complexity only when needed (summarization, then memory formation)
For chat applications: Keep 10-15 recent messages verbatim, summarize older content every N turns (N=10-20 typical)
For agents: Extract key facts (decisions, constraints, goals) to separate memory, use recent actions + facts for context
Implement token counting BEFORE sending requests - proactively manage context, don't wait for failures
Test summarization quality - verify summaries retain critical information (user intent, decisions, constraints)
Consider use case: Customer support needs longer history; quick Q&A can use minimal context
Monitor metrics: Track average context size, summarization frequency, user corrections indicating lost context
